title: Bootstrap Navbar & Navigation
description: Learn how to build responsive navigation bars with Bootstrap so visitors can move around your website easily.

sections.heading: Creating a Navbar
sections.explanation: A navbar is a navigation bar that helps users move around your site. In Bootstrap, you add the class navbar to a nav element. The navbar-expand-lg class makes the menu spread out on large screens. You can place a navbar at the top of any page.
sections.code: Navbar content goes here.

sections.heading: Adding a Brand
sections.explanation: The brand is usually the name or logo of your website. You add it with a link that has the class navbar-brand. This link appears on the left side of the navbar. Clicking the brand normally takes the user back to the homepage.
sections.code: My Website

sections.heading: Navbar Links
sections.explanation: Links inside a navbar use the class nav-link. Group them inside a container with the classes nav and navbar-nav. You can also add the active class to highlight the current page. The disabled class makes a link unclickable.
sections.code:
• Home
  • About

sections.heading: Responsive Toggle Button
sections.explanation: On small phones, the navbar links hide behind a toggle button. The button shows only when the screen is small. You use the navbar-toggler class for the button. The data-bs-toggle attribute switches the menu open and closed.

sections.heading: Navbar Color Styles
sections.explanation: Bootstrap gives you color classes for the navbar. The classes navbar-light and navbar-dark control the text color. You can also add background color classes like bg-dark or bg-primary. This helps your navbar match your website design.
sections.code: My Site

title: Bootstrap Cards, Images & Badges
description: Use Bootstrap cards, images, and badges to present content in clean boxes with eye-catching labels.

sections.heading: Creating a Basic Card
sections.explanation: A card is a flexible box that holds content like text and images. Bootstrap cards use the class card. You place content inside it with the class card-body. Cards are useful for showing information in a neat box.
sections.code: This is a simple card.

sections.heading: Adding a Card Title
sections.explanation: Cards look better when you add a title and text. The card-title class styles a heading inside the card. The card-text class is used for paragraphs. These classes add the right spacing and size automatically.
sections.code:
Card Title

Some text inside the card.

sections.heading: Card with Image
sections.explanation: You can put an image at the top of a card. Place the image before the card-body. Use the class card-img-top to make the image fit the card width. Text stays below the image this way.
sections.code: Photo description.

sections.heading: Adding Badges
sections.explanation: Badges are small labels that show extra information. You create one with the badge class. The classes bg-primary or bg-success set the badge color. Use a span tag to keep the badge on the same line as text.
sections.code:
Inbox 5
Messages 3
Alerts 2

sections.heading: Cards in a Row
sections.explanation: You can place cards side by side using the grid. Wrap the cards in a row and give each card a column class. Bootstrap divides the row into twelve equal parts. Each card takes up part of the width.
sections.code:
Card One
Card Two

title: Bootstrap Modal & Alerts (JavaScript Components)
description: Create popup modals and alert messages with Bootstrap JavaScript components to interact with users.

sections.heading: Building a Modal
sections.explanation: A modal is a popup window that appears on top of the page. It needs a container with the class modal. The dialog inside uses the class modal-dialog. Content goes inside a section with the class modal-content.
sections.code: Modal body text here.

sections.heading: Modal Header and Footer
sections.explanation: A modal usually has a header, a body, and a footer. The header holds the title with the class modal-title. The body uses the class modal-body. The footer holds buttons like Close and Save.
sections.code:
New Message

Modal body content.

sections.heading: Opening the Modal
sections.explanation: You open a modal by clicking a button. The button needs the data-bs-toggle attribute set to modal. The data-bs-target attribute points to the modal id. Use a hash symbol before the id in the target.
sections.code:
<button type='button' class='btn btn-primary'
  data-bs-toggle='modal' data-bs-target='#myModal'>
  Open Modal
</button>

sections.heading: Dismissible Alerts
sections.explanation: Alerts show a short message to the user. You make one with the classes alert and alert-warning. To let users close an alert, add alert-dismissible. Add a button with the class btn-close at the end.
sections.code: Please check your details.

sections.heading: Alert Colors
sections.explanation: Bootstrap offers alert styles in many colors. Use alert-success for success messages. Use alert-danger for errors and alert-info for useful tips. The colored background makes messages easy to see.

title: Bootstrap Carousel
description: Build an image slideshow carousel with controls, indicators, captions, and autoplay.

sections.heading: Setting Up a Carousel
sections.explanation: A carousel is a slideshow that cycles through images. It needs a container with the classes carousel and slide. Add the id carouselExample to connect its parts. Every image belongs inside a carousel-item div.

sections.heading: Adding Controls
sections.explanation: Controls are buttons that let the user move between slides. Add a button with the class carousel-control-prev for going back. The data-bs-slide attribute tells Bootstrap which direction to go. Each control needs both prev and next buttons.

sections.heading: Carousel Indicators
sections.explanation: Indicators are small dots that show the current slide. They sit at the bottom of the carousel. Each dot is a button with the class carousel-indicators. The active class shows which slide is on screen.

sections.heading: Adding Captions
sections.explanation: Captions place text on top of a slide image. Wrap the text in a div with the class carousel-caption. The text appears in the middle or bottom of the image. This is useful for adding titles to slides.
sections.code:
Welcome

Our featured offer for today.

sections.heading: Autoplay and Pause
sections.explanation: A carousel moves automatically every few seconds. You can use pause hover to stop it when the mouse is over it. Set ride to carousel to start moving on page load. These are useful data attributes for the carousel.

title: Bootstrap Icons & Typography
description: Add Bootstrap icons and improve your text with typography and alignment utility classes.

sections.heading: Using Bootstrap Icons
sections.explanation: Bootstrap Icons is a free set of small images for your pages. You load it with a link in the head of your page. Each icon is drawn with a span tag. The icon name goes in the bi class.

sections.heading: Icon Sizes
sections.explanation: Icons come in different sizes for different places. Use the fs classes from Bootstrap to make them bigger or smaller. Lower fs numbers like fs-1 make the icon the largest. You can also change the color with text classes.

sections.heading: Display Headings
sections.explanation: Display headings are extra-large titles for hero sections. Use the classes display-1 to display-6. Lower numbers make bigger text. They stand out more than normal headings.
sections.code:
Display One

sections.heading: Text Utilities
sections.explanation: Bootstrap text classes style words quickly. The classes text-center, text-white, and text-uppercase do common jobs. Use text-muted for light gray helper text. These classes work on any text element.
sections.code:

sections.heading: Lead Text and Emphasis
sections.explanation: The lead class makes a paragraph a little larger. It is perfect for the opening sentence of a page. Bootstrap also gives you classes for bold and italic text. Use fw-bold for bold and fst-italic for italic.

title: Bootstrap Building a Complete Page Layout
description: Combine Bootstrap parts into one complete page layout with a header, hero, grid sections, and footer.

sections.heading: Page Container
sections.explanation: A container centers your content on the page. The class container makes a fixed-width box. The class container-fluid uses the full width. Many pages start with one container to hold everything.
sections.code: My Bootstrap Page

sections.heading: Navigation and Grid
sections.explanation: Combine a navbar and a grid to build page structure. The grid uses rows and columns to divide space. Columns add up to twelve across a row. Here the page has a navbar and two columns.

sections.heading: Hero Section
sections.explanation: A hero is the big welcome area at the top of a page. It often has a large heading and a button. You can style it with background and padding classes. The button uses the btn btn-primary classes.

sections.heading: Content Sections
sections.explanation: Long pages use several sections with headings. Each section can use the row and col grid again. Add a my-4 class for breathing space around sections. This keeps the layout tidy and easy to read.

sections.explanation: A footer sits at the bottom of the page. It often contains copyright text and small links. Bootstrap text utilities make it easy to style. A dark background class works well for footers.
